sections.body: Before deciding, try 'steelmanning': state the other side's argument in its strongest form. If you can't, you may not understand it yet.
Ask: Who is affected? What would they say? What evidence would change my mind?
ESTIMATION ('back of the envelope'): break a big question into smaller guessable parts.
Example: how many heartbeats in a day? About 70 per minute × 60 minutes × 24 hours ≈ 100,000.

options: Stating the other side's best version of their argument
hints: It's the opposite of a 'straw man'.
Steel is strong; straw is weak.
A straw man twists an argument to make it weak. A steel man does the opposite.
quiz.explain: Steelmanning means presenting the strongest version of the other side's argument.

quiz.q: Estimate: about how many minutes are in a week?
hints: Minutes in an hour × hours in a day × days in a week.
Seconds in an hour = 60 × 60 = 3,600. Use the same multiply-up method.
